items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 23 at 11:46AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
A cold front is currently moving northwest to southeast across
the North Slope. As the front reaches the Brooks Range,
precipitation begins as rain then transitions to a mix this
afternoon/evening. There is uncertainty with exact precipitation
types, but Anaktuvuk Pass should mix with snow and freezing
drizzle between 3 PM and 5 PM resulting in a glaze of ice on
elevated surfaces as temperatures drop near freezing this evening.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 23 at 11:46AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
A front moving across the Arctic Coast today will bring rain
showers which transition to a wintry mix this evening. The chances
for a wintry mix increase from 5PM to 11PM tonight. This wintry
mix can be sleet, snow and freezing drizzle. After midnight
Thursday night, the steadiest and heaviest precipitation should
transition to a mist or freezing drizzle which can result in
patchy ice, especially on colder/elevated surfaces. Otherwise,
Friday will be chilly with patchy ice possible in the mornin
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:43PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Water levels will rise slightly with each high tide Wednesday
night through Friday morning. The highest water level rises will
be in Eastern Norton Sound, around 1 to 3 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water level rises around 0.5 to 1.5 feet are
expected from Golovin to Nome.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
